title: Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Repairer
raw_text:
10-15E. MOS 15E—Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Repairer CMF 15 (Rescind 202610)
     a. Major Duties. The Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Repairer performs, inspects, and
supervises TUAS field and sustainment maintenance. Troubleshoots and repairs the aircraft electrical,
avionics, communications, propulsion, fuel system, and takeoff and landing systems. Removes and
replaces payload and weapons systems to include electrical and mechanical components. Troubleshoots
and repairs the ground control and support equipment to include electronic and communication systems.
Prepares TUAS related maintenance forms and records.
Duties for MOS 15E at each level of skill are:
       (1) MOSC 15E1O. Troubleshoots and repairs TUAS electrical, avionics, communications,
propulsion, fuel system, and takeoff and landing systems according to applicable manuals, directives, and
safety procedures. Removes and installs tactical unmanned aircraft system subassemblies. Performs
inspections and periodic maintenance on the aircraft, ground control equipment, associated ground
support equipment, and takeoff and landing systems. Performs aircraft fueling/de-fueling and arming/de-
arming operations. Serves as a crewmember performing launch and recovery operations. Performs
alignments and calibrations on tactical unmanned aircraft systems. Maintains facilities for storage of
flammable and hazardous materials. Requisitions and maintains shop and bench stock for repair of
aircraft systems and equipment. Uses and performs operator maintenance on tools, special tools and
aircraft ground support equipment. Prepares forms and records related to aircraft maintenance.
       (2) MOSC 15E2O. Performs duties described in paragraph a.(1), supervises, and provides
technical guidance to subordinate personnel while performing quality control duties. Monitors flammable
and hazardous material control and storage. Schedules maintenance on test, measurement and
diagnostic equipment (TMDE). Alters or modifies material according to approved modification work
orders.
       (3) MOSC 15E3O. Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel
performing duties described in paragraphs a(1) and a(2) and evaluates the aviation maintenance training
program (AMTP). Evaluates maintenance operations and facilities for compliance with directives,
technical manuals, work standards, safety procedures, and operational policies. Performs maintenance
trend analysis and applies production control, quality control and other maintenance management
principles and procedures. Computes weight and balance and ensures compliance with aircraft
configuration control, Army Oil Analysis Program, and TMDE calibration. Instructs personnel and
conducts technical training in TUAS electrical, avionic, communications, propulsion, fuel, payload and
weapon systems repair procedures, and shop and flightline safety. Monitors requisition of parts, tools,
and supplies.
       (4) MOSC 15E4O. Manages and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing
duties described in paragraphs a(1), a(2), and a(3) and manages and evaluates the AMTP. Manages
TUAS maintenance and production control activities. Determines man-hours, personnel, parts, and facility
requirements to repair TUAS and associated equipment. Coordinates maintenance areas, component
repair, technical inspection techniques, and procedures according to directives, technical manuals, work
standards, and operational policies. Manages supply economy and discipline. Manages the TUAS quality
control training program. Prepares evaluations, special reports and records pertaining to TUAS
maintenance and related activities.
           b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award or reclassification of MOS.
             (1) The Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Repairer must possess the following
qualifications: Waivers, and/or exceptions must be approved by Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft
Rucker, AL 36362-115000, (https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted).
                 (a) Physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
                (b) A physical profile of 222221
                (c) Normal color vision.
                (d) Qualifying scores.
                    (1) A minimum score of 93 in aptitude area EL and 104 in aptitude area MM.
                    (2) A Minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) -0120 cm, Seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles in
Physical Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
                (e) A security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to maintain the
MOS.
                (f) A U.S. Citizen.
                  (g) Formal training (completion of MOS 15E under the auspices of The United States Army
Aviation Center of Excellence (AVCOE) is mandatory.
                 (h) Reclassification: Must meet the above qualifications and all prerequisites IAW AR 614-
200” Reclassification of primary military occupational specialty and/or secondary military occupational
specialty” chapter and AR 40-501 “Medical Fitness Standards for Retention and Separation, including
Retirement” chapter. . Must be in the grade of SPC (non-promotable) or below unless they have held an
aviation maintenance/component repairer CMF 15 MOS or MOS 15M for a minimum of 12 months at skill
level 1 or 2, 18 months at skill level 3.
                    1. Active Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
waiver packet to Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft Rucker, AL 36362-5000,
(https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted)
                    2. National Guard: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
waiver packet through National Guard Bureau, ATTN: NGB-ARNG-AV, 111 South George Mason Drive,
Arlington, VA 22204-1382, (http://www.rucker.army.mil/usaace/directorates/cdid/opfd/iw_enlisted.html).
                    3. Reserve Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit
a waiver packet through Commander, Army Reserve Aviation Command (ARAC), ATTN: G3 (AFAK-
OPT), 1160 Brandenburg Station Road, Ft Knox, KY 40121-4190, (usarmy.usarc.arac.list.g-37-
training@army.mil).
             (2) MOS closed for reclassification to Soldiers who have been deemed permanently non-
deployable in accordance with AR 40-501, AR 220-1, AR 600-8-101, and AR 614-30. Soldiers must meet
the minimum criteria for retainability stated in AR 635-40, paragraph 3-5(a) and be fully deployable to all
locations and echelons.
     c. Additional skill identifiers. Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
enlisted MOS).
     d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
       (1) Table 10-15E-1. Physical requirements.
       (2) Table 10-15E-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
       (3) Table 10-15E-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
